title: iPhone 18 Series Launch: 7 Things Buyers Need to Know Before Upgrading
excerpt: Apple's big iPhone event skipped the phone most people actually buy, raised prices on everything else, and introduced a $1,999 foldable. Here's the story, and what it means for your upgrade.
content:
Apple's latest iPhone launch has a strange gap in it: there is no iPhone 18. Not yet, anyway. Apple announced only the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and a first-ever foldable called iPhone Duo, then raised prices on its older models. Here's what that means for your upgrade.

Quick verdict: iPhone 17 Pro owners can probably skip this one. If you're on an iPhone 16 Pro or older and want the best camera, look at the iPhone 18 Pro. If you wanted a regular iPhone 18, there isn't one yet.

Researched September 28, 2026. Not affiliated with Apple. Details will be updated as Apple confirms more, so bookmark this page.

## What Apple launched

- iPhone 18 Pro: from $1,199 in the US. On sale September 18 (Confirmed by Apple).
- iPhone 18 Pro Max: from $1,299 in the US. On sale September 18 (Confirmed by Apple).
- iPhone Duo foldable: from $1,999 in the US. Pre-orders October 16, on sale October 23 (Confirmed by Apple).
- Standard iPhone 18: not launched. MacRumors reports it's coming in spring 2027, but Apple hasn't confirmed that (Reported).

## What changed

The main upgrade is the camera. The main lens now changes its aperture, from ƒ/1.48 to ƒ/4 according to Engadget, so it can take in more light at night or keep more of a group photo sharp. There's also a faster A20 Pro chip, faster charging and better battery life. Apple rates the Pro at up to 36 hours of video playback and the Pro Max at up to 45, against 33 and 39 hours on last year's models, per Engadget.

The design is nearly the same. BGR says you'd struggle to tell it from the 17 Pro apart from the colors.

## The price catch

The new Pros cost $100 more than last year's. MacRumors, 9to5Mac and AppleInsider also report that Apple raised US prices on the iPhone 16, 17, 17e and Air by $100 each and discontinued the 17 Pro. Waiting for a discount on last year's model doesn't work this year. The price of the future standard iPhone 18 is unknown.

## Should you upgrade?

- iPhone 17 Pro owner: keep your phone. Engadget and TechRepublic both say the gains are small.
- iPhone 16 Pro or older: BGR says the 18 Pro is the phone to get.
- Regular iPhone buyer: wait for spring if your phone works. If it doesn't, the iPhone 17 is the newest standard model.
- Curious about the Duo: wait for full reviews. Only hands-on impressions exist so far, and NeoTeo reports it weighs 254g.

Reviewers also note that some 18 Pro units freeze after a failed Face ID attempt. Apple has confirmed a software fix is coming, according to 9to5Mac.

## For Sri Lankan buyers

Sri Lanka isn't among the countries Apple named for launch, and Apple hasn't published an official Sri Lankan price. Local listings we found ranged from LKR 559,000 (LuxuryX) to LKR 690,000 and up (iSpot). Those are retailer prices, not official ones.

Apple's headline battery figures are for eSIM-only models, sold in 12 markets that don't include Sri Lanka. A SIM-tray version likely rates lower, though we didn't find Apple's exact figure. Before you pay, check the SIM version, who provides the warranty, and the all-in price from two or three sellers.

## Final verdict

The iPhone 18 Pro is a solid camera and battery upgrade for people on an iPhone 16 Pro or older, and a skip for 17 Pro owners. The Duo is an expensive first attempt that deserves full reviews before you spend $1,999. Everyone waiting for a regular iPhone 18 is in limbo until a reported spring event. If this helped, share it with a friend who's deciding.

Sources: Apple Newsroom, Engadget, BGR, TechRepublic, MacRumors, 9to5Mac, AppleInsider, NeoTeo, LuxuryX, iSpot.
